vid_sm_sd2: In this video I bake a simple sourdough loaf. The float test tells you the starter is ready: drop a spoonful in water and it should float. Do stretch and folds every 30 minutes for the first 2 hours. A long cold proof in the fridge overnight gives more flavour and an easier score. Bake in a preheated dutch oven, lid on for 20 minutes, then lid off. Subscribe for more bread!
vid_sm_sd4: Hydration matters: 75% hydration gives an open crumb but is harder to shape. Use strong bread flour with high protein. Let the bulk ferment go until the dough has risen about 50%. Wet hands stop the dough from sticking.
vid_sm_md1: Motion design builds on the classic principles. Ease in and ease out so movement starts and stops gently, never linear. Use anticipation: a small move the other way before the main action. Overlapping action makes shapes feel loose: parts arrive a few frames apart.
vid_sm_md3: Plan the piece as a storyboard before you open After Effects. Use the graph editor to shape your easing curves. Pre-compose groups of layers to keep the timeline clean. Render a quick preview at half resolution to check timing.
vid_sm_cg1: Always correct before you grade: fix white balance and exposure first. Use scopes, not your eyes, because your monitor can lie. The waveform shows brightness; the vectorscope shows saturation and hue. Grade in nodes: one node per change.
vid_sm_cg3: Step one: balance the shot. Step two: set the contrast with a gentle S curve. Step three: add a look with a LUT at low opacity. Step four: isolate the subject with a power window. Step five: match every shot of the scene.
vid_sm_st2: You do not need a gym to get stronger. Pick 5 compound moves: goblet squat, Romanian deadlift, row, press and lunge. Do 3 sets of 8 to 12 reps. Stop one or two reps before failure. Sleep and protein matter as much as the workout.
vid_sm_sl1: Wake up at the same time every day, even on weekends. Get bright light in the first hour after waking. Stop caffeine 8 to 10 hours before bed. Keep the bedroom cool, dark and quiet.
vid_sm_sl3: A short nap of 20 minutes can boost focus without hurting night sleep. Nap before 3pm. Long naps can leave you groggy and make it harder to fall asleep later.
vid_sm_bu2: Zero-based budgeting gives every dollar a job, so income minus spending equals zero. Plan the month before it starts. Include irregular costs like gifts and car repairs as monthly amounts.
vid_sm_bu4: Put cash for each spending category in its own envelope. When the envelope is empty you stop spending in that category. It works best for groceries and eating out.
vid_sm_hp2: Snake plants, ZZ plants and pothos cope with low light. Low light means slower growth, so they need less water. Rotate the pot every few weeks so the plant grows evenly.
vid_sm_ru1: Land with your foot under your hips, not far in front. Aim for a cadence of about 170 to 180 steps per minute. Keep your shoulders relaxed and your arms swinging forward and back.
vid_sm_ru3: Start with run-walk intervals: 1 minute running, 1 minute walking. Run three times a week with a rest day between. Good shoes fitted at a running shop prevent a lot of pain.
vid_sm_bl1: Apply the scale with Ctrl A before you add modifiers, or bevels look wrong. Keep the topology clean with quads. Use the subdivision surface modifier instead of adding real geometry. Save often and turn on auto save.
vid_sm_bl3: Eevee renders in real time and is great for previews and stylised work. Cycles traces light paths, so it is slower but gives realistic shadows and reflections. Use denoising in Cycles to cut render times.
vid_sm_sr1: Do dynamic stretching before a workout: leg swings and arm circles warm you up. Save static stretching for after, holding each stretch for 30 seconds. Never bounce in a static stretch. Stretching every day improves flexibility faster than long sessions once a week.
vid_sm_wc2: A flat wash needs plenty of paint mixed before you start. Tilt the board so a bead of paint forms at the bottom of each stroke. A gradient wash adds more water to each stroke as you go down.
vid_sm_wc3: Too much water makes blooms and cauliflowers. Dab your brush on a towel to control how wet it is. Wet on wet gives soft edges; wet on dry gives sharp edges.
vid_sm_co1: Mix greens and browns: food scraps are greens, dry leaves and cardboard are browns. Aim for about three parts browns to one part greens. Turn the pile every week to add air. Keep it as damp as a wrung-out sponge.
vid_sm_co3: A bad smell means too many greens or too little air. Add browns and turn the pile. A healthy compost smells like soil.
